title: The Border of Geneva
premise: Marguerite Winterbourne, a veteran air-crash investigator, has spent two decades chasing the truth of the accident that killed her family in row twelve — an investigation repeatedly buried by rewritten rules and sealed files. When her long-dead handler sends a meeting invitation for tomorrow, she walks into a trap that entangles her with a Russian defector who may be bait for the same conspiracy that downed Flight 4471. As she extracts the defector across Europe, she discovers the crash was staged to silence a witness whose testimony now lives only in the defector's memory. In the end, Marguerite must choose between publishing the truth and protecting the found family of survivors and defectors who have become her new row twelve.
about_author: Mirabel Halloran is a former aviation safety analyst who left the field after a decade of investigating accidents no one wanted explained. She writes thrillers from a farmhouse near Geneva, where she keeps a wall of unclaimed passenger photographs.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Twenty years after the crash, she re-reads the final report on the anniversary, noting a new revision that quietly changes the cause. The emotional beat is grief sharpened into professional suspicion; she notices the rewrite bears her own old case number.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. An encrypted message arrives from Aldous Vane, her handler who died three years ago, summoning her to a Geneva café tomorrow at noon. She verifies his death certificate herself. The beat is dread laced with hope — the dead do not send calendar invites.

chapters.title: Café du Rhône
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the meeting she finds not Vane but Ilya Sorokin, the defector, who claims Vane arranged this before dying and passes her a keycard in Vane's handwriting. A surveillance team enters. The beat is vertigo: the trap has already sprung around her.

chapters.title: Extraction Protocol
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Relying on crash-site instincts, she moves Ilya through Geneva's tram network using dead drops she hasn't touched in years. They reach a safehouse as it burns behind them. The beat is adrenaline masking the realization someone inside the agency is hunting them.

chapters.title: What Ilya Knows
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. He reveals he was a records clerk who memorized and destroyed documents proving Flight 4471 was downed to kill a whistleblower aboard — possibly in row twelve. The beat is terrible intimacy: he may hold her family's death sentence in his head.

chapters.title: The Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She cross-references twenty years of amended reports and finds each revision erased one detail: seat assignments, cargo manifests, a second transponder. The beat is cold fury as pattern recognition becomes personal indictment.

chapters.title: Deputy Director Reyes
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Inside the agency, Deputy Director Reyes learns Marguerite has the keycard and orders containment, framing her as unstable. The beat is institutional menace — the antagonist believes he is protecting order, not committing murder.

chapters.title: Safehouse in Annecy
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Hiding at a lakeside cottage owned by Odile, a retired colleague, Marguerite and Ilya begin reconstructing the memorized documents. The beat is fragile warmth — the first stirrings of found family between investigator, defector, and reluctant host.

chapters.title: Ghost Signal
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A message arrives in Vane's cipher: coordinates and the word 'row twelve.' Either Vane lives or someone has his keys. The beat is haunted compulsion; she knows it may be bait but cannot refuse.

chapters.title: The Hangar
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At a decommissioned hangar she finds the reconstructed fuselage section of 4471 — including row twelve, preserved, with evidence of an incendiary device never reported. The beat is visceral confrontation with her family's last minutes.

chapters.title: Ambush at Dusk
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Reyes's team raids the hangar; Ilya escapes through maintenance tunnels while Marguerite is captured buying him time. The beat is guilt and sacrifice — the defector becomes the protector.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Held in a black site, she faces Reyes, who offers her the official truth in exchange for Ilya and silence. He admits the crash was sanctioned but insists it saved thousands. The beat is moral vertigo — the villain's arithmetic almost adds up.

chapters.title: Odile's Network
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Odile activates a quiet network of retired investigators and exiles who owe her favors, planning Marguerite's extraction. The beat is solidarity — strangers becoming family out of shared unfinished grief.

chapters.title: Twenty Minutes Over the Lake
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The extraction goes wrong when a mole in Odile's network tips Reyes; a boat chase across Lake Geneva ends with Odile wounded shielding Ilya. The beat is costly victory and the shattering of their temporary sanctuary.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, escaped during the chaos. She identifies the traitor by a detail only a report-rewriter would know — the same phrasing used across twenty years of amendments. The beat is betrayal confirmed and method revealed.

chapters.title: Vane's Vault
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Following Vane's cipher to a bank vault, she finds his posthumous insurance: recordings proving Reyes ordered the cover-up, plus a letter confessing Vane faked his death to finish the investigation. The beat is grief transmuted into inheritance — the dead handler's legacy handed over.

chapters.title: Countermove
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Cornered, Reyes plans to destroy the vault records and stage Ilya's death as espionage, closing every thread. The beat is tightening noose — the antagonist's desperation makes him more dangerous and less careful.

chapters.title: The Press Conference Gambit
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Rather than flee, she schedules a public briefing of crash-victim families, knowing Reyes must act in the open. The beat is defiant courage — turning her twenty years of ritual mourning into a weapon.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Revisited
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the briefing, Reyes attempts to arrest her mid-testimony; families stand, recordings play, and the preserved fuselage evidence surfaces via Odile's network. The beat is cathartic climax — private grief made public truth.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV then Marguerite's. Exposed, Reyes tries to flee via private airfield; Marguerite confronts him on the tarmac, choosing arrest over vengeance. The beat is moral resolution — she refuses to become the thing that killed her family.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Months later, Ilya testifies before an international commission, his memorized documents corroborated by Vane's recordings. The beat is release — memory finally honored instead of hunted.

chapters.title: The New Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At a lakeside memorial, Marguerite sits with Odile, recovering, and Ilya — her found family — and finally reads her family's true names into the record. The beat is bittersweet peace: the border of grief crossed, inheritance reclaimed.
